nodes.label: No-Gods Screenshot — Goose Voting Carousel
nodes.description: Screenshot of the GooseOS goose art voting carousel. Displayed inside a Win95-style window titled 'belle-lettres.exe', the UI shows a 3-panel meme-style collage of Canada geese with overlaid text captions: 'He attacc' (repeated three times) and 'But most importantly'. Below the image carousel are left/right navigation arrows and a caption reading: 'one goose dared to love. All he ever wanted was a warm embrace... but fate made him a weapon'. The Windows 95 taskbar with a Start button is visible at the bottom of the screen. The overall color palette is gray/muted, consistent with Win95 desktop styling.

nodes.label: Goose Art Voting Carousel UI
nodes.description: The voting carousel component visible in the screenshot. Allows users to browse goose art submissions using left/right arrow navigation. Each item shows an uploaded image with an associated caption/description. Implemented in carousel.js as part of the GooseOS legacy frontend.

nodes.label: belle-lettres.exe Win95 Window
nodes.description: A Win95-style window frame wrapping the voting carousel, titled 'belle-lettres.exe'. Rendered by the GooseOS window manager system. Includes standard Win95 chrome: title bar with minimize/maximize/close buttons, gray bordered window body.

nodes.label: 'He Attacc' Goose Meme Submission
nodes.description: A user-submitted goose art piece displayed in the voting carousel. Composed of three photos of Canada geese attacking / charging, with meme-style caption text overlaid: 'He attacc' (top), 'He attacc' (middle), 'But most importantly' (bridge), 'He attacc' (bottom). Accompanied by the flavor text: 'one goose dared to love. All he ever wanted was a warm embrace... but fate made him a weapon'. This is the content displayed in the 'no-gods' screenshot state.

nodes.label: Win95-Style Taskbar with Start Button
nodes.description: The Windows 95-style taskbar visible at the bottom of the GooseOS desktop in this screenshot. Contains a Start button on the left. Part of the GooseOS desktop environment chrome implemented by window-manager.js.
